messages:
Raj: heads-up — after the kernel-selector change merged last night we're seeing a regression on Mistral-8x hosted endpoints. p99 increased ~12% and tail GPU busy looks spikier. Noticed this from the nightly perf job (compare against yesterday's baseline).

Sasha: thanks — do we have a perf profile/trace? can you paste the flamegraph or nvprof snippet?

Raj: attaching quick profiler excerpt below (trimmed). this is a 1k token chat request with streaming off:
```
GPU time by op:
  attention_kv_gemm      18.2ms
  ffn_gemm               9.6ms
  kv_cache_write         1.1ms
  softmax                2.3ms
  overhead (launcher)    6.8ms
Total per-step ~38ms vs baseline ~33.6ms
```

Mike: hmm launcher overhead up ~2.5ms, and attention_kv_gemm jumped ~3ms. Kernel selector recently started preferring the new tiled GEMM for int8 path, right? could be a bad tile size for Mistral shapes.

Anita: also saw a small regression on Qwen when we adjusted RoPE scaling to support longer contexts last week. That change touches rotary params at KV dim -> could change which kernel we hit if the implementation has special-case paths for certain head dims.

Priya: +1 on kernel tile mismatch. For Mistral-8x our per-head KV dim is nonstandard (head_dim=64 but kv_dim=128 in some fused checkpoints) — selector heuristics assume head_dim==kv_dim in a lot of rules. If selector falls back to a generic GEMM kernel instead of the optimized fused kernel, perf drops.

perf-bot: perf-regression alert: job=nightly-inference, model=mistral-8x, delta_p99=+12.1%, run=1718431200 -> flagged. See /perf/alerts/1718432100

Sasha: can you reproduce locally with a focused harness? script like:
```bash
python perf_harness.py --model mistral-8x --prompt samples/1000tok.json --batch 1 --no-stream --profile nvtx
```
If it repros, capture the kernel selection decision log by setting `RUNTIME_DEBUG=kernel_select` then paste the snippet.

Raj: repros locally. kernel select log shows we switched from `fused_kv_gemm` -> `tiled_gemm_v2` for the attention path. Reason: tiled_gemm_v2 was marked lower-latency for int8 shapes after the quant batch tests, but the test set didn't include Mistral's KV layout. snippet:
```
[selector] model=mistral-8x head_dim=64 kv_dim=128 dtype=int8 -> chosen tiled_gemm_v2 (score=0.72)
[selector] fallbackable kernels: fused_kv_gemm (score=0.68), generic_gemm (score=0.55)
```

Mike: that scoring delta is small; our confidence threshold allowed swap. Short-term: pin a per-model kernel override in model-config for Mistral-8x to force `fused_kv_gemm`. Medium-term: add a microbenchmark in the kernel CI that includes Mistral-like kv shapes so selector learns correct ranking.

Anita: we should also check batching heuristics — yesterday's change bumped the dynamic batch window from 8ms -> 18ms for throughput stabilization which increases aggregation for short queries but hurts tail latency for single-turn chats. The nightly workload is dominated by short 20-40 token prompts; bigger batches amplify the kernel runtime delta at p99.

Priya: addition: tokenizer artifacts are contributing to token count variance. We saw increased byte-fallback tokens for emoji-heavy prompts in the nightly corpus. That inflates token lengths and changes sequence-length distribution feeding the kernel selector heuristics. Example: user message with multi-byte chars -> `byte_fallback` adds 3-6 extra tokens. This changes batching profile and Kv cache pressure.

Raj: good catch. Also found a subtle prompt-formatting issue: our chat template was adding both a BOS and an extra system EOS marker for some legacy adapters, doubling the special-token overhead in certain flows. Fixing that reduces average token count by ~1.8 tokens per request in repro.

Sasha: action list proposal:
- short-term (hotfix): model-config override for mistral-8x to prefer `fused_kv_gemm` and restore dynamic batch window to 8ms for hosted pool (canary 10%)
- medium: expand kernel microbenchmarks to cover head/kv dim mismatches (head_dim!=kv_dim), and include RoPE-scaled Qwen shapes in selector training set
- long: add tokenizer histogram in the console to track byte-fallback and special-token inflation per route, plus prompt lint rules to avoid duplicate BOS/EOS markers

Mike: implemented the config override in a branch. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/req/2154 — it toggles per-model kernel_preference and emits a metric `kernel_override_active`. Will canary now.

Anita: also instrumented KV cache churn metric: `kv_cache_evictions/sec` — before fix it's ~0.2/s per-session, after change it jumps to 1.1/s for long chats due to mispredicted seq-len. Tracking in console.

Raj: thanks team. I'll roll the hotfix to 10% canary and keep an eye on p99 and GPU flamegraphs. If canary looks good we promote. I'll follow up with a short postmortem summary in #eng-runtime after we confirm baseline restored. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: canary rollout started: 10% cluster -> monitors on. will report final after 30m.
